implication: A Reg 31(4) disclosure is the mandatory public announcement of a proposed or completed substantial acquisition (typically ≥25% of capital); this triggers the open offer obligation and defines the offer price, timeline and settlement mechanics for all public shareholders.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Mandatory public disclosure of substantial acquisition (acquisition leading to ≥25% shareholding) or takeover intent; must include acquirer, shareholding details, offer price and timeline.
Definition of 'substantial acquisition' and trigger thresholds (≥25% of voting capital or ≥2% in any financial year); determines applicability of open offer.
Open offer obligation: acquirer must make a mandatory open offer to acquire shares from public shareholders at the higher of negotiated price or weighted average price.
Minimum public shareholding requirement post-acquisition (normally 25%); exemptions may apply for certain sectors or structures.
Board approval and shareholder consent (if required) for capital restructuring and share issuance or acquisition; concurrent review with takeover notice.
Continuous disclosure obligations during the acquisition period; material related-party transactions and material developments must be announced.
If the acquirer is a non-resident or foreign entity, FDI/FII approval from RBI/FIPB may be required depending on sector and acquirer nationality.
CCI approval required if the transaction triggers deal-value or combined-turnover thresholds (currently ₹2,000 cr combined assets); sugar milling may be caught depending on group footprint.

headline: Davangere Sugar Company Limited files Regulation 31(4) disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulations
sum: Davangere Sugar Company Limited has submitted a Regulation 31(4) disclosure to NSE, indicating a substantial acquisition of shares or an open offer announcement under the SEBI Takeover Regulations 2011.
detail: The company has filed the standardised disclosure form required under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, with the National Stock Exchange of India. This disclosure is the gating step in any takeover or substantial acquisition involving a listed Indian company, and must include details of the acquirer, the number and price of shares being acquired, the rationale, funding sources and the timeline for the mandatory open offer to public shareholders. The specific acquisition details (acquirer identity, share count, consideration and offer price) are contained in the filed disclosure document, which is the operative legal instrument.
